contentHtml:
If you're looking for a 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary that makes the most of every hour without leaving things to chance, you're in the right place. The Huasteca Potosina packs waterfalls, turquoise rivers, caves and archaeological sites into a fairly compact area, which makes it possible to see its highlights over a long weekend. With the right planning, three days are enough to get a full picture of the region.

The biggest mistake first-time visitors make is trying to improvise a Huasteca Potosina route without knowing the opening hours, entrance fees or real distances between sites. A well-planned 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary lets you organize your stops in a logical order, avoid unnecessary drives and save time to enjoy the water instead of rushing from place to place. Individual entrance fees in 2026 range from $60 MXN at the Tamasopo Waterfalls to $220 MXN + $300 MXN panga per person at Tamul Waterfall, so it's also smart to have your budget clear before you leave.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. If you'd rather hand off the logistics, you can book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina directly with our trusted operators.

Day 1 and Day 2: the Huasteca Potosina route of waterfalls and caves

Day 1 — Tamul, Cueva del Agua and your first time on the river

Day one kicks off with Tamul Waterfall (Cascada de Tamul), the tallest in San Luis Potosí, with a 105-meter free fall. Admission is $220 MXN + $300 MXN panga per person, and you get there by paddling a boat up the Tampaón River, a trip of about 40 minutes that's already part of the experience. In the afternoon, Cueva del Agua (Water Cave) offers an underground contrast with crystal-clear water; it's the stop on the way back on the Tamul Expedition, which for $1,550 MXN per person also includes the waterfall and the Sótano de las Huahuas. If you're traveling on your own, check availability in our activities in the region. To stay nearby without wasting time on drives, see the options in lodging near the Huasteca waterfalls 2026.

Day 2 — Sótano de las Golondrinas and the Micos Waterfalls

Day two brings together two very different experiences. The Sótano de las Golondrinas, in Aquismón, is one of the deepest pit caves in the world; admission is $100 MXN, and the sight of thousands of birds flying out at dawn is unlike anything else. In the afternoon, the Micos Waterfalls (Cascadas de Micos), at about $100 MXN per person, offer a series of stepped falls that are perfect for swimming and ziplining. This stretch is a centerpiece of any serious plan for what to see in the Huasteca in 3 days.

Day 3: Tamasopo, Puente de Dios and wrapping up your 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary

Tamasopo Waterfalls in the morning

The Tamasopo Waterfalls are open daily from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and admission is $60 MXN per person. Getting there before 9:00 a.m. means fewer crowds and better light on the water. The natural pools let you swim in different current levels. If you want to know when the water flow is at its best, see the guide on the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina.

Puente de Dios before heading home

A few minutes from Tamasopo is Puente de Dios ("God's Bridge"), with admission at $150 MXN per person. The stone arch over the river creates a turquoise chamber that gives any Huasteca weekend trip a strong finish. Combining both sites in the same morning is completely doable if you leave early.

Practical tips for your Huasteca Potosina trip

  • Budget: Our 3-day, 2-night package with a hotel in Xilitla, Huasteca Immersion, costs $8,699 MXN per couple. See all the options in available activities and tours.
  • Season: October through January combines good water flow and mild temperatures. Read more in the guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026.
  • Total cost: To work out entrance fees, meals and transportation, see the guide on how much it costs to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026.
  • Footwear: Wear water sandals with non-slip soles. The paths have stretches of wet, slippery rock.
  • Cash: Most ticket booths and boatmen don't take cards. Bring enough cash from Ciudad Valles or Tamasopo.

Frequently asked questions about a 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary

Is a 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary enough to see the main sites?

Yes, with three well-planned days you can visit Tamul, Cueva del Agua, Sótano de las Golondrinas, Micos, Tamasopo and Puente de Dios. The key is to stick to opening hours and avoid doubling back between places in the Huasteca Potosina.

How much money do I need for a Huasteca weekend trip?

For entrance fees alone, plan on about $1,000 MXN per person for the six main sites (the Tamul panga is most of it). If you add lodging, food and transportation, a budget of $2,500–$3,500 MXN per person is reasonable for an independent three-day trip.

What should I see in the Huasteca in 3 days if I'm traveling with young kids?

The Tamasopo Waterfalls and Puente de Dios have safe swimming areas, and kids under 3 get in free. Tamul is also family-friendly. Skip the Sótano de las Golondrinas with very young kids because of the uneven paths.

Is it better to book an organized package or do the Huasteca Potosina route on your own?

Our packages with hotel, from $8,699 MXN to $16,500 MXN per couple, include the hotel in Xilitla, breakfast on tour days, the tours and transportation from the hotel to each one; getting to Xilitla is up to you, and the package simplifies the logistics. Traveling on your own is cheaper if you have your own vehicle, but it takes more advance planning of routes and schedules.
